summary: Amwill is an asset-light dermatology and cosmeceutical marketer, not a proprietary-drug discovery platform. At the dated ₹44.55 close, its ₹89.12 crore market value is modest against ₹57.83 crore March cash/deposits and profitable operating activity. This creates a conditional, price-led value thesis rather than an established compounder thesis. BQS 5.40, Growth Quality GQS 6.45 and IAS 6.45 place it in the speculative or mixed-quality watchlist cell. The decisive strength is funding resilience; the decisive risks are historical near-single-distributor dependence, opaque current customer concentration, treasury risk allocation and very weak trading liquidity. The financed base produces 27.07% annual return, but linked severe stress loses about 59% of the entry value. Verified collections, treasury holdings/capital-call obligations and executable trading conditions would change the practical conclusion more than a promotional product announcement. [S1, RHP, AUG, SEP, M1]

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Amwill is an asset-light dermatology and cosmeceutical marketer, not a proprietary-drug discovery platform. At the dated ₹44.55 close, its ₹89.12 crore market value is modest against ₹57.83 crore March cash/deposits and profitable operating activity. This creates a conditional, price-led value thesis rather than an established compounder thesis. BQS 5.40, Growth Quality GQS 6.45 and IAS 6.45 place it in the speculative or mixed-quality watchlist cell. The decisive strength is funding resilience; the decisive risks are historical near-single-distributor dependence, opaque current customer concentration, treasury risk allocation and very weak trading liquidity. The financed base produces 27.07% annual return, but linked severe stress loses about 59% of the entry value. Verified collections, treasury holdings/capital-call obligations and executable trading conditions would change the practical conclusion more than a promotional product announcement. [S1, RHP, AUG, SEP, M1]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Amwill Health Care Limited, BSE 544353, ISIN INE0U2L01017; BSE SME, not an NSE operating listing merely because its BSE security appears in the interoperability master. Information cutoff October 20, 2026. The observed secondary close is ₹44.55 on October 19, with 20,003,600 issued shares and ₹89.1160 crore market value. Lot 1,200 costs ₹53,460. Financial scope is standalone Indian GAAP, with no subsidiary consolidation. Horizon ends October 19, 2031, five years after the reference close; equity return hurdle 15%; liquidity reference ₹5 lakh, not a recommended allocation. [S1, SEC, M1]

G1 Integrity is Conditional: disclosed controller economics, Amderma relationship change and treasury allocation need monitoring, but reviewed records do not establish diversion. G2 Reliability is Conditional: the signed financial opinion is unmodified after testing restored/reconstructed records; the separate inability to conclude on backup/audit-trail compliance is retained, not erased. G3 Funding is Conditional: dated liquid resources cover the modeled base and severe operating needs, but investment permissions do not establish actual liquidity or available redemption. G4 Tradability is Conditional: dated trades establish activity, but L1 reflects a long exit period and absent live depth/full BSE restriction verification. [S1, E7, AUG, SEP, M1]

Evidence confidence is Medium for history, governance, growth decomposition, capital returns and valuation inputs. The cyber event reduces confidence in the original record trail, not automatically in every audited aggregate: alternative audit procedures explicitly support those aggregates. No current distributor/customer split or fully reconciled treasury capital-call ledger was found. These are modeled as operating and asset-recovery uncertainties rather than silently assumed away. High return uncertainty is separate from confidence in what the filings actually say. The October 23 results meeting is after the cutoff; no unreported September result is used.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors: GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 4, BAL 8, EXEC 5 and EARN 6. IAS factors are R 10, D 4, P 7 and L 1. Each factor has an evidence-linked judgment, contrary evidence and Medium confidence in the audit objects.

BQS = 0.20×5 + 0.20×4 + 0.12×8 + 0.10×6 + 0.12×5 + 0.10×4 + 0.08×8 + 0.08×5 = 5.40. GQS = 0.40×8 + 0.20×6 + 0.15×6 + 0.15×5 + 0.10×4 = 6.45. IAS = 0.25×5.40 + 0.35×10 + 0.20×4 + 0.10×7 + 0.10×1 = 6.45. Coverage is 100% of required factors; no weights are renormalized. No critical gate override is triggered on the reviewed evidence.

The preferred five-year 20.37% revenue CAGR starts REV at 8; no bonus is awarded for a strong recovery off the FY2021 loss-year base. CASH 4 reflects poor multi-year conversion but improving recent realization. It is not assigned 3 and then arbitrarily exempted from a cap: the recovery and investing classification of treasury interest are substantive contrary evidence. Thus no persistent CASH/CAP override caps GQS. R 10 follows the base 27.07% return less the 15% hurdle, a 12.07-point spread. L remains 1 even before any downgrade for missing live depth. Numerical scores describe this conditional framework, not a guarantee that a ₹5 lakh order can be implemented.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Amwill develops/formulates and markets dermatological products using third-party manufacturers and a physician-oriented field force. It sells products rather than earning a recurring software-like subscription. Manufacturing, logistics and clinical advice depend on outside counterparties; the prospectus explicitly said there was no in-house R&D department. The annual report describes collaboration with formulation and manufacturing experts, not evidence of a new owned research platform. FY2026 sales were ₹45.4923 crore in one pharma-products segment, entirely India. [RHP, S1]

FY2026 category mix is led by hair care 26.62%, dry skin 18.38% and skin lightening 13.85%, together 58.85%; anti-acne is 12.02%, sunscreen 7.26% and anti-fungal 5.91%. Karnataka is the leading state; the annual state chart does not provide an auditable numerical concentration table, so no state-share percentages are invented. June 2025 management reported entry into Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, North East India, Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh, with new sales leadership and representatives. That is management’s expansion account, not independently measured productivity. [S1, E11]

Historically Amderma Healthcare LLP was the dominant carrying-and-forwarding/distribution counterparty: disclosed FY2024 revenue share 98.96% and September 2024 half-year 98.35%. The January 1, 2024 agreement described up to 4% margin, 60-day payment or mutual agreement and a four-year term, with 60-day termination rights. The annual related-party classification ends March 15, 2025. Zero FY2026 related sales therefore does not establish that the distribution dependency disappeared. Current ownership/control and actual customer concentration remain unresolved. Cash collection, not merely invoiced sell-in, is central to the thesis. [RHP, H25, S1]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible advantage is a small portfolio of prescriber-recognized brands, product presentation and field relationships. Repeat skin/hair usage can sustain demand and outsourced manufacturing limits fixed-asset intensity. These benefits are contestable: the prospectus acknowledges unsuccessful/discontinued products, dependence on external dermatologists and manufacturing replacement risk. No verified exclusivity, market-share leadership or patent estate supports a durable-monopoly conclusion. [RHP, S1]

Eris is a useful operating comparator because it markets branded formulations including dermatology, but its FY2026 consolidated revenue of ₹3,129 crore, six manufacturing sites and broad stockist/retail network make it radically larger and more diversified. Its 35.8% EBITDA margin is not automatically an Amwill target. Sun Pharma’s official India catalogue includes hair-restorer, skin-care and dermatological alternatives, illustrating competitive substitution. Sun’s global specialty, manufacturing and R&D economics are not a matched valuation peer. No current peer P/E is borrowed to price Amwill. The model’s 7/10/14-times terminal operating NOPAT range is an explicit small-company valuation assumption tested down to 5, not a claimed observed peer discount. [ERIS, SUN]

MOAT 4 balances useful brand relationships against limited verified differentiation, concentration and dependence on contracted capabilities. Better independently evidenced prescription traction, diversified channels and stable pricing without increased promotional expense would support a higher assessment; generic industry growth would not.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Revenue in ₹ crore for FY2021–26 is 17.9994, 27.6132, 30.1663, 43.9483, 40.5816 and 45.4923. Annual additions are +9.6138, +2.5531, +13.7820, −3.3667 and +4.9107 crore. Five-year CAGR is 20.37%; three-year FY2023–26 CAGR 14.68%; latest growth 12.10%. FY2026 is only 3.51% above FY2024 despite the headline five-year trajectory. [DRHP, RHP, H25, S1]

The FY2021 endpoint is a full company financial year after the March 2020 promoter-proprietorship asset transfer, not a partial-year stub. The older draft and final prospectus agree on overlapping FY2022/23 revenue, providing a comparability check. The five-year measure is therefore used, with its low-base and pandemic-period context retained. A PAT CAGR from the FY2021 loss is NM, not a growth statistic. No subsequent acquisition revenue is identified in the reviewed scope; this does not independently prove every rupee is volume-led. Price, mix, new territories and product launches are not quantitatively decomposed. [DRHP, RHP]

June 2025’s regional hiring and sunscreen launch offer a plausible bottom-up growth mechanism. October 2026’s CDSCO approval permits FoliColor hair-colour import through October 2031 unless suspended/cancelled; it does not disclose purchase orders, contracted volume or a revenue amount. The base uses 12% annual sales growth close to the latest reported pace, the bear 2%, the bull 20% and severe −5%. None is management guidance. [E11, E1]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Expansion can proceed through additional representatives, prescriber coverage, geographic distribution and product introductions rather than a large owned factory. That makes the business less capex-heavy but not capital-free: receivables and commercial spending absorb funds, and current debtor days exceed the prospectus’s nominal 60-day payment term. Contractual flexibility may explain part of the gap; it is not evidence of fictitious sales, but warrants collection monitoring. [RHP, S1]

The base annual model funds working capital at 45% of annual sales and maintenance/asset-light expansion capex at 1.5% of sales. Its EBIT margin is 25%, below FY2026’s 27.36% core EBIT margin, leaving a cost allowance for the field force and product development. The bull requires 20% growth, 28% margin and 2% capex, not simply a higher terminal multiple. No unannounced plant or guaranteed product success is inserted. No external equity or borrowing is needed under the modeled base, bear, bull or severe paths, given the dated financial assets; this result does not certify future treasury redemption rights.

Operating returns are strong on a small asset base, but most equity is held in deposits/investments and future private-credit returns are unverified. GQS 6.45 therefore reflects meaningful but unproven scaling potential, not a compounder designation. Preserving low capex while allowing debtor days to rise indefinitely would not be high-quality growth. Evidence of renewed supplier/collection dependence or investment losses would lower the reinvestment assessment even if headline sales rise.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Tarun Gandhi and Anand Gandhi each held 31.64% at March 2026; the promoter group held 70.65%. Combined managing-director remuneration was ₹3.144 crore, unchanged from FY2025 and about 27.5% of FY2026 PAT. Related office rent and deposits are disclosed. The statutory auditor states remuneration complied with requisite approvals; a high economic share is not by itself an illegality allegation. The FY2025 increase from combined ₹1.8956 crore FY2024 is material to the earnings bridge. [S1, H25]

Amderma’s related-party classification ended March 15, 2025 and Ample Pharma’s March 22. Reviewed annual notes do not provide a complete ownership/control-change bridge or the continuing distributor sales share. This is a precise transparency gap, not evidence that the relationship ended operationally or that a prohibited transaction occurred. IPO fresh proceeds were ₹48.88 crore and OFS ₹11.10 crore; OFS money did not belong to the company. The IPO and remuneration should be judged together with subsequent operating cash generation and capital allocation. [RHP, H25, S1]

Promises versus delivery: June 30, 2025 described new territories, field-force hiring and sunscreen launch; FY2026 sales grew 12.1%, but regional profitability and representative productivity are not disclosed. January/June/August/September 2026 approved broader investment allocations; these are permissions, not proof of returns or complete deployment. October 10 disclosed a new import approval; commercial sales remain to be demonstrated. [E11, E9, E6, AUG, SEP, E1]

The February 18 notice said accounting data from September 30 was affected but compliance-related data remained secure. April’s update subsequently disclosed loss and reconstruction of structured-database entries from July 31, 2025 to February 18, 2026. That later disclosure qualifies the initial broad assurance; the reviewed record does not explain the change or establish intent. The later, more specific disclosures take precedence. April’s company-secretary certificate confirms re-entered UPSI entries using supplied records but explicitly disclaims an independent forensic audit. The later financial auditor tested reconstructed accounting records through alternative procedures and gave an unmodified financial opinion. It nevertheless could not conclude daily-backup and audit-trail operation/preservation compliance. These scopes must be kept distinct. No allegation of manipulation or intentional data destruction is made. [E7, E8, S1]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Historical standalone ₹ crore, FY2021 / FY2022 / FY2023 / FY2024 / FY2025 / FY2026:
Revenue: 17.9994 / 27.6132 / 30.1663 / 43.9483 / 40.5816 / 45.4923.
PAT: −0.9980 / 2.5737 / 3.1144 / 12.5363 / 10.7301 / 11.4213.
CFO: 0.0709 / 3.0181 / 4.7919 / −3.0552 / 5.5640 / 8.0028.
Cash capex: 0.8032 / 0.1107 / 0.3147 / 0.8913 / 0.7158 / 0.5848.
FCF proxy, CFO less capex: −0.7323 / 2.9074 / 4.4772 / −3.9465 / 4.8482 / 7.4180. This excludes treasury investment transactions, which must be assessed separately. [DRHP, RHP, H25, S1]

Core EBIT, PBT less other income, is ₹16.4283 / ₹11.1960 / ₹12.4470 crore for FY2024–26. Corresponding EBITDA is ₹16.6669 / ₹11.6510 / ₹12.9926 crore. FY2024’s sharp margin increase included lower salaries despite higher revenue; the prospectus quantifies the wage/PF reduction but does not establish a durable efficiency mechanism. FY2025’s current tax of about ₹1.1977 crore was net of IPO-expense tax impact under note 14.3. The printed note ends without quantifying the adjustment, visually verified; this is not an unexplained low-tax allegation. The model uses 25.168% recurring tax and does not extrapolate the IPO benefit. FY2026 other income ₹2.9191 crore is mainly deposit interest ₹2.8612 crore, not operating brand earnings. [RHP, H25, S1]

Three-year CFO/PAT is ₹10.5116/₹34.6877 = 30.3%; FY2022–26 ₹18.3216/₹40.3758 = 45.4%. Normalizing PAT to operating NOPAT still leaves only about 35.1% three-year conversion before allocating treasury-related taxes. Latest-year conversion is improving: CFO ₹8.0028 crore versus core NOPAT about ₹9.3144 crore; adding the estimated tax attributable to non-operating income gives operating CFO about ₹8.7375 crore. That analytical tax allocation is not a reported cash-flow subtotal. [S1, H25, RHP]

FY2024’s negative CFO reflects ₹11.7242 crore receivable absorption and ₹4.8920 crore lower payables, not capex. FY2026 receivables absorb another ₹4.1798 crore and close at ₹20.9012 crore. Average receivable days rise from 133.5 to 150.9; most balances are reported below six months, with ₹0.0464 crore older than six months. Inventory is only ₹0.8295 crore. A small overdue bucket does not eliminate channel concentration or extended-credit risk. [RHP, S1]

Committed operating capital, defined as operating working capital plus PPE/development and operating security deposits, is ₹13.6807 / ₹18.4109 / ₹21.1086 crore for FY2024–26. FY2026 core NOPAT divided by average FY2025–26 capital is 47.1%; one-year incremental NOPAT/incremental capital is 34.7%. Older negative operating-capital denominators, supplier financing and major changes in cash holdings make five-year/three-year incremental ratios unreliable as project returns; they are not scored as spectacular infinity. These estimates exceed a reasoned 12–16% operating capital-cost range, distinct from the 15% equity hurdle, while total-equity ROE is only 14.17%. [S1, H25, RHP]

March cash/bank ₹47.3719 crore plus long deposits ₹10.46 crore total ₹57.8319 crore. Separate investments are government bonds ₹2.3590 crore book/₹2.2738 crore market and Vivriti units ₹0.1504 crore. The bond is pledged to a broker; it is not immediately free operating cash. Net tax provision ₹1.0586 crore and book overdraft ₹0.0828 crore settle once. The FY2026 dividend ₹1.00018 crore is deducted as a pre-entry obligation. IPO note 39 reports full use of the designated allocations; ₹0.529 crore escrow reimbursement relates to issue costs already internally paid, not a new expense. It remains inside the model’s cash floor until reimbursement. No cash is counted twice as an investment. [S1, E3, AUG, SEP]

The primary capital note and official dated master agree on 20,003,600 issued shares. Historical EPS is affected by the IPO and weighted-average denominator: FY2026 EPS ₹5.71 versus ₹6.63 FY2025 is not inconsistent with higher total PAT. No additional unissued warrant capital is identified in the reviewed disclosures. No contingent liabilities or capital commitments were disclosed at March; subsequent investment authorizations are considered separately, not assumed absent.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹44.55 and 2.00036 crore shares, market value is ₹89.1160 crore, about 7.8 times FY2026 PAT. Combining that price with dated March cash/FD/investments produces an indicative operating EV near ₹28.86 crore before tax/dividend and liquidity adjustments, about 2.2 times core EBITDA. This is explicitly a dated-balance diagnostic, not a verified current enterprise value or immediate liquidation proceeds. [S1, M1]

The annual model separates operating EV, retained cash and financial assets. It starts from March and rolls all operating cash once through FY2027–31 and an exact FY2032 stub to October 19, 2031. Thus the pre-entry March–October period is an estimate pending September results, not an extra cash balance added twice. No future dividend receipts are assumed; retained cash appears at exit. Minimum cash is ₹2 crore. Hypothetical emergency debt of up to ₹5 crore at 12% includes half-year new-draw interest, followed by equity at a 30% price discount with 5% friction if needed. None is assumed committed, and none is required in the displayed four paths.

Base transfers ₹8.8496 crore from deposits into a ₹9 crore risk-treasury bucket including the existing ₹0.1504 crore investment. This deliberately tests full draw of the identified January/June/September private-credit approvals, not an assertion that all were deployed or non-overlapping commitments. It earns zero modeled AIF distributions. Government bonds are separately valued at March market value; deposit/bond cash yield is an estimated 6%, not an assertion of exact coupon receipts. Alternative allocation paths include no further draw, ₹6 crore, ₹15 crore loss and the entire mixed ₹33 crore mandate. September’s approval sits within August, not on top of it. [E9, E6, AUG, SEP]

Base: sales grow 12% annually, EBIT margin 25%, WC 45% of sales, capex/depreciation 1.5%, terminal operating NOPAT multiple 10. Terminal operating EV ₹167.9861 crore plus cash ₹116.0066 crore, bond ₹2.2738 crore and risk assets ₹9 crore gives equity ₹295.2665 crore, or ₹147.61/share, a 27.07% annual return. Bear: 2% growth, 16% margin, WC 55%, multiple 7, ₹2 crore receivable impairment and treasury losses gives ₹63.75/7.43%. Bull: 20% growth, 28% margin, WC 40%, capex 2%, multiple 14 gives ₹273.21/43.72%. These are conditional scenarios, not target prices with assigned probabilities.

Sensitivity: a 7-times base multiple gives ₹122.41/22.40%; 20% EBIT margin gives ₹123.16/22.55%; WC 60% gives ₹140.15/25.76%; ₹5 crore receivable impairment gives ₹144.55/26.54%. Full ₹33 crore mixed-mandate deployment with 50%/100% principal loss gives ₹136.04/25.02% and ₹127.79/23.46%. A 15% margin plus 5-times multiple gives only ₹73.52/10.54%; 20% margin plus 5-times yields ₹89.57/14.99%, around the hurdle. These joint operating sensitivities are more consequential than treating every deposit as riskless.

Base 15% hurdle entry is ₹73.39; bear’s is about ₹31.70. This broad range, not a single buy price, represents uncertainty. In the base structure even roughly 6% annual revenue contraction can meet the hurdle because retained financial assets are large; that reverse result depends on maintaining the assumed margin and asset value, not a free-money conclusion. AIF principal may remain illiquid at exit, and governance/holding-company-like discounts to financial assets are relevant. No matched-current peer multiple or independent portfolio NAV audit eliminates that risk.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest objection is that apparent cheapness combines a difficult-to-exit share with financial assets whose deployment and ultimate shareholder distribution are not independently verified. A distributor disruption can reduce sales, require a replacement channel and lengthen collections precisely while private-credit/redemption losses reduce funding flexibility. High book cash does not establish a cash tender or distributable surplus. [RHP, S1, AUG, SEP]

Severe stress links 5% annual sales contraction, 5% EBIT margin, WC at 65% of sales, ₹10 crore receivable impairment, a 75% loss on a fully deployed ₹33 crore mixed treasury mandate, another ₹2 crore deposit/financial-asset impairment and a 5-times operating NOPAT exit. It yields ₹18.28/share and −16.32% annual return, about 59% permanent value loss versus entry. The ₹33 crore bucket is not described as an AIF authorization: it represents all approved investment categories. Haircuts are hypothetical tests, not allegations of losses already incurred.

Receivable impairment reduces opening WC; required replacement investment then absorbs cash once. It is not deducted again as a fictional immediate payment. Financial-asset haircuts reduce recoverable principal rather than adding an unreported operating expense. No financing is required in this severe path, but survival of the company is not protection against minority-shareholder impairment. A documented materially unreliable revenue/cash trail, actual undisclosed encumbrance or inability to collect the dominant channel would change the gate assessment, not merely the price target.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
The thesis is not sold as a 5×/10× compounder. At the base 25% margin, 45% WC and 10-times exit NOPAT, the fully funded reverse model requires approximately 24.44% annual sales growth for a 5× quoted-price outcome and 44.29% for 10×. These are above the latest 12.10% growth, and 10× is far above the 20.37% five-year recovery CAGR. Higher required sales also fund higher working capital and capex; the result is not an unfunded P/E multiplication.

The modeled bull exceeds 5× only because it combines 20% growth, 28% margin and a higher 14-times exit multiple. It is an optimistic conjunction, not independent evidence of likely multibagger performance. Durable prescriber traction, diversified collections, productive reinvestment and sensible financial-asset stewardship would all be needed. Without those, low initial valuation alone is insufficient.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Treasury holdings and calls: baseline March cash/FD ₹57.8319 crore and separate investments ₹2.5094 crore; reconcile the next portfolio statement to January/June/August/September permissions. A deployment outside disclosed limits or material unknown encumbrance is a gate-review event, not an assumed present fact.
2. Collections: baseline average debtor days 150.9 and receivables ₹20.9012 crore. Improvement toward the prior 133.5 days supports the thesis; a sustained move beyond the modeled 55–65% WC stress or material aged balances requires reassessing revenue quality and return.
3. Distributor exposure: obtain current Amderma ownership/control and sales share before claiming diversification. A documented channel termination or material collection default invokes the linked downside model immediately.
4. Core margin: baseline FY2026 EBIT 27.36% of sales, base 25%, bear 16%. Persistent erosion toward 20% combined with a low exit multiple makes the hurdle borderline; loss of underlying earning power matters more than treasury-supported PAT.
5. Growth delivery: FY2026 12.10%; verify regional and product revenue before extrapolating the June 2025 expansion or October import permission. A licence alone is not a sales milestone.
6. Cash realization: recent CFO ₹8.0028 crore and FCF proxy ₹7.4180 crore should be reconciled with non-operating interest and tax. Renewed negative operating cash alongside rising receivables is an investigation trigger.
7. Record integrity: review the next audit’s backup/audit-trail conclusions and evidence of durable remediation. A financial qualification affecting material revenue/cash, unlike the current scoped compliance limitation, may change G2.
8. Implementation: recheck lot, current restrictions, live spread/depth and turnover for the actual intended position. The current observed-only 5% participation exit estimate is 24.25 sessions; an occasional large print does not establish capacity to sell. Research cadence is at the next results/disclosures, not an automated monitoring commitment.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
With BQS 5.40 and IAS 6.45, the canonical classification is Speculative or mixed-quality watchlist. Growth Quality GQS 6.45 does not upgrade the business into an established compounder. This is a conditional value setup whose possible return comes from a low entry price and financial assets, not proof of superior governance or defensible market leadership.

Research action: prioritize verification of current treasury holdings/calls, continuing distributor economics and collections. Implementation action: no portfolio-sized purchase or exit recommendation is made. L1 and the absence of live execution data are substantial constraints even though the intrinsic scenario appears attractive. The illustrative ₹5 lakh position is not a suitability recommendation. At different prices, recalculate IAS from the same economic paths rather than altering BQS to fit market performance.

Actual treasury loss, distributor failure or a financial reliability qualification could lower scores/change gates. Stronger verified diversification and cash realization could improve business quality. A price increase alone can exhaust the apparent return margin without improving the business; around the ₹73.39 base hurdle entry the base return is only 15%, while the bear supports much less.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Core primary hierarchy: FY2026 signed annual statements and audit [S1]; FY2025 annual and tax note [H25]; final prospectus [RHP] for FY2022–24 and distribution terms; May 2024 draft [DRHP] only for the overlapping-checked FY2021 extension. Signed investment, cyber, AGM and licence attachments [E1/E3/E4/E5/E6/E7/E8/E9/E11, AUG, SEP] supply dated events. BSE attachments were read through exact-document public mirrors where direct BSE access failed; those remain primary issuer documents, not secondary article claims. Eris/Sun sources are operating comparisons only. The source ledger contains direct links and specific locators.

Price and OHLCV [M1] are secondary; official interoperability master [SEC] supports identity, lot and issued capital, not BSE surveillance clearance. The recent 20-session window is used for implementation because it is after the disclosed August dividend; the older 60-session observations cross that action and are not blindly combined as unadjusted turnover. Missing rows are not treated as zero. Low×volume is a calculated turnover bound, not measured exchange traded value.

Unresolved: current Amderma ownership/control and sales mix; exact current treasury holdings, capital calls, redemption terms and any new pledges; independently verified regional/product economics; and complete live BSE restrictions/depth. No auditor or government source examined establishes misconduct. The scope-specific cyber caveats are not suppressed. FY2025 IPO-tax impact is directionally disclosed but not fully quantified in the printed note.

Major analyst assumptions are growth, EBIT margin, WC, capex/depreciation, treasury yield/recovery and exit NOPAT multiple. Annual financing, exact terminal stub, impairment reconciliation, no-double-count cash bridge, reverse cases and sensitivities are preserved in the linked model and reproducible audit. Supported estimates are used rather than leaving avoidable freshness gaps as blanket NS; their uncertainty is shown explicitly. The financial assets are not promised to be distributed or liquid at the model’s terminal date.

gates.reason: Disclosed controller remuneration, historical dominant related distributor and its unbridged classification change warrant caution. Treasury approvals are explicit but do not establish productive stewardship. No reviewed evidence establishes severe diversion or illegal remuneration.

The unmodified signed financial opinion follows alternative audit testing of restored/reconstructed books. Separate backup/audit-trail compliance limitations and the non-forensic SDD certificate remain explicit. These do not establish that material financial aggregates are unreliable; Medium-confidence aggregate inputs and adverse sensitivities support numeric IAS, subject to the next audit and cash verification.

Dated cash/deposits, separately valued financial assets and operating cash fund all four modeled paths without borrowing/equity. IPO escrow reimbursement stays within the cash floor and authorized investment transfers are deducted from cash before adding investments. Current deployment, capital calls and redemption terms are not fully verified, so no unconditional availability claim is made.

Observed recent trades and the 1200-share lot support conditional assessment, but observed-only median turnover already implies 24.25 sessions for a 5 lakh exit at 5% participation. Missing rows are not zero-filled; live depth and complete BSE restrictions are not verified. L1 reflects very poor implementation rather than a fabricated suspension.

limitations: Current Amderma ownership/control and continuing revenue share are not independently reconciled; zero related-party sales does not establish channel diversification.
Current treasury deployment, complete capital-call obligations, redemption terms and new encumbrances are unverified. Authorizations are not represented as actual investments.
The FY2025 printed tax note attributes an IPO-expense benefit but does not quantify the complete bridge; recurring tax is normalized.
Original accounting logs were partly lost; the financial opinion is unmodified after alternative procedures, but backup/audit-trail compliance could not be concluded.
Regional sales productivity and price/volume mix are not independently decomposed; new import approval is not a revenue order.
Five-year incremental operating-return ratios are not meaningful on older negative operating-capital denominators; a transparent latest-year proxy and total-equity return are provided.
No refreshed matched-peer market-multiple table is established. Operating comparisons and explicit intrinsic valuation sensitivities are used.

Secondary turnover bounds are not official traded value. Seven dates are absent in 60 sessions, two in the latest20; no missing dates are treated as zero. Latest20 observed-only statistics avoid relying on the August dividend-crossing window.
No live spread/depth or comprehensive BSE surveillance clearance; liquidity score and IAS are conditional on the reference position.

score_note: Completed conditional annual financed analysis. No severe persistent CASH/CAP override is applied; recovering recent cash realization is explicitly weighed against weak multi-year conversion. Numeric IAS is conditional on a 5 lakh reference position and L1 implementation risk.

GOV.reason: March promoter group holds 70.65% and two managing directors receive 3.144 crore combined remuneration, while historical dominant distributor Amderma ceased related-party classification on March 15, 2025 without a reviewed ownership/control bridge. Audited RPT disclosure and explicit investment approvals are counterweights; no diversion or illegal remuneration is established.

MOAT.reason: Physician relationships, registered brands and a differentiated product mix create commercial value, but manufacturing is outsourced and the prospectus discloses no in-house R&D department and unsuccessful discontinued products. Sun and Eris demonstrate strong substitutes and distribution advantages. No verified patent monopoly or sustainable pricing power supports a high moat score.

REV.reason: Comparable five-year revenue CAGR is 20.37% from 17.9994 crore FY2021 to 45.4923 crore FY2026, starting 8 with no adjustment. Three-year CAGR is 14.68%, FY2025 contracted 7.66%, and FY2026 growth is 12.10%. No post-base acquisition inflates the series; price/volume decomposition is not verified.

DUR.reason: Dermatology, repeat hair/skin care and documented geographic expansion provide demand access; October import approval adds an option. Yet historical single-distributor dependence, physician acceptance and competition constrain the runway, and an import permission is not an order or revenue guarantee.

CAP.reason: Asset-light operating ROIC is approximately 47.1% on average FY2025–26 committed operating capital, and the latest incremental proxy is 34.7%. However FY2026 reported ROE is only 14.17%, treasury absorbs most equity and approved private-credit allocations have no verified realized returns. Negative older operating-capital denominators prevent extrapolating a clean multi-year project-return series.

CASH.reason: FY2024–26 cumulative CFO/PAT is 30.3% and five-year FY2022–26 conversion 45.4%; receivable days rose from 133.5 to 150.9. Counterevidence is recovery of CFO from negative 3.06 crore to positive 5.56 and 8.00 crore, and positive recent FCF. Treasury interest sits outside CFO while related tax remains inside, so latest operating conversion is better than raw CFO/PAT. Mixed conversion warrants 4, not a persistent-severe override.

BAL.reason: March cash and deposits of 57.8319 crore exceed known operating obligations, and even the linked severe case requires no modeled external equity or debt. Treasury risk, pledged long-duration bonds and collection concentration prevent calling all balances risk-free or immediately distributable; 33 crore full-limit loss sensitivities are explicit.

EXEC.reason: The June 2025 regional expansion and product launch are followed by FY2026 sales recovery and higher core EBIT, but revenue remains only 3.5% above FY2024 and pre-IPO peak margin has not returned. Cyber reconstruction was audited through alternative procedures, while independent proof of complete original logs is absent.

EARN.reason: Core EBIT rose from 11.196 crore FY2025 to 12.447 crore FY2026, distinct from rising treasury interest. FY2024 core EBIT was 16.4283 crore, FY2025 tax benefited from IPO expenses, and FY2026 EPS 5.71 remains below prior 6.63 after IPO dilution. These limit extrapolation of reported profit growth.

R.reason: Conditional base terminal price 147.61 implies 27.07% annual return, 12.07 percentage points above the 15% hurdle. At 7 times terminal NOPAT return remains 22.40%; the lowest 15% margin/5 times sensitivity gives 10.54%, showing parameter dependence rather than certainty.

D.reason: Base balance-sheet strength prevents a funding failure in modeled stress, but coupled 5% annual revenue decline, 5% EBIT margin, slower collections, 10 crore receivable impairment and 75% loss on a fully deployed 33 crore treasury mandate reduce terminal value to 18.28, about 59% below entry. Cash stewardship and distributor failure can impair permanent value.

P.reason: Issued market value is 89.116 crore, about 7.8 times FY2026 PAT. Dated March cash/investments make normalized operating EV unusually low, and base hurdle entry is about 73.39. This is a price-led value case, not proof of a cash-distribution arbitrage; no refreshed matched-peer multiple establishes the exact exit valuation.

L.reason: Latest 20-session window has 18 secondary observations. Using observed-only median low×volume 412320 rupees gives 24.25 days for a 5 lakh reference position at 5% participation, already over 20 days without assuming missing dates are zero. Lot 1200 costs 53460 rupees; unobserved depth/restrictions and participation impact can worsen implementation.

assumption_basis.scope: Standalone only. No subsidiaries. Annual FY2027–31 and exact FY2032 stub to 19 October 2031. FY2027 includes the estimated March-to-entry roll-forward because no September results are yet published; no pre-entry dividend is counted as a future investor receipt.
assumption_basis.treasury: Base assumes all identified January, June and September private-credit approvals add to 9 crore, rather than claiming this was actually deployed. This is a conservative allocation path, not an asserted outstanding commitment. September sits within August’s 33 crore overall mandate. Alternative paths cover overlap/no further draw and full-limit losses. AIF distributions are zero in the model and terminal principal is a separately exposed value, not operating earnings capitalized at the business multiple. The government bond uses March market value and a modeled 6% cash yield on that value, not an assertion of the contractual coupon cash amount; it stays separately pledged, and no liquidation is needed to fund base operations.
assumption_basis.operating: 12% base sales growth is close to FY2026 12.1%, rather than extrapolating the 20% five-year recovery. Base 25% EBIT margin is below FY2026 normalized 27.4%. Capex equals depreciation at 1.5% revenue as a maintenance/replacement and modest asset-light expansion allowance; product development and field-force costs remain in the operating margin. No separate plant ramp is invented.
assumption_basis.risk_bucket: The 33 crore stress is the full mixed August mandate, not a claim of 33 crore AIF authority. It includes debt, equity/IPO, private credit, invoice discounting and mutual funds. Haircuts are hypothetical correlated loss tests, not expected losses or an allegation of loss already incurred.
assumption_basis.funding: Net tax due, book overdraft and declared FY2026 dividend settle once outside operating WC. The 0.529 crore IPO reimbursement is an internal cash classification, not a second issue expense. The 0.529 crore escrow amount remains within the 2 crore cash floor until reimbursement; it is not assumed immediately distributable. Minimum cash 2 crore; hypothetical debt capacity 5 crore at 12% plus half-year new-draw interest, then equity at 30% price discount with 5% issue friction. Neither is assumed sanctioned. All future surplus retained; future dividends are not promised.

confidence.forecast: Wide business and treasury outcomes; evidence confidence is not forecast certainty.
